notes: Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (PDF in Downloads; Table 1 read from the page image). author: Adelaar, Alexander
title: Malagasy phonological history and Bantu influence
notes: Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (Project MUSE PDF in Downloads). A critique of Wolff's (2010) treatment of Malagasy. §2.3 states the changes in three stages: Proto-South East Barito (PSEB1-9, Table 3, p. 131, premigratory, shared with the SEB languages of Kalimantan), Proto-Malagasy (PMLG1-4, Table 4, p. 135, postmigratory) and the dialects (MLG1-4, Table 5, p. 136; Merina MRN1-4, Table 6, p. 138); §3 the spirantization of stops and semivowels, §4 the retroflex affricate tr, §5 the reduction of nasal + stop clusters, §6 PAN *s; §7 Bantu (Sabaki, Comorian) contact. Data sources in the Appendix (pp. 155-156): Maanyan from Dahl (1951), Merina from Webber (1853), Richardson (1885) and Abinal & Malzac, South Sakalava from Gueunier (n.d.), North Sakalava from Thomas-Fattier (1982), Bara from Elli (1988), South Betsimisaraka from Ruud (1955), Old South Betsimisaraka from Flacourt (1658), Old Taimoro (Sorabe script) from Ferrand (1904). Malagasy written in its orthography with o as u, ŋ for the velar nasal, paragogic vowels with a breve and stress marked; PAN and PMP in Blust's ACD notation with ə for *e.

author: Adelaar, Alexander
title: Malagasy dialect divisions: Genetic versus emblematic criteria
notes: Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (Project MUSE PDF in Downloads). Reviews Dez (1963), Vérin, Kottak & Gorlin (1969), Mahdi (1988), Gueunier (1988), Simon (2006), lexicostatistics and the Levenshtein method (§3), and proposes criteria for a genetic classification (§4): *li and *ti, final *t (Tables 1-6), *y > z and *w > v (Table 7), the merger of final-syllable *i and *e (Table 8), the personal prefixes *i and *ra-, numeral compounds, <in>, voice and lexical taxonomy. Tentatively a Northern-Central-Eastern branch against the southwestern dialects; the place of the western dialects is open (pp. 476-477). Malagasy in its orthography with o as u, final y as i, paragogic vowels with a breve, ŋ; PMP for PAN.

author: Goodenough, Ward H.
title: Gradual and quantum changes in the history of Chuukese (Trukese) phonology
notes: Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (JSTOR PDF in Downloads). Compares the vowels of Kiribati (Bingham 1908), Woleaian (Sohn & Tawerilmang 1976) and the Romónum dialect of Chuukese (Dyen 1949; Goodenough & Sugita 1980) to argue that change is gradual phonetically and abrupt phonemically. PMc kept the five POc vowels, POc *u having a central [ɨ] and a back [u] allophone (Dyen 1949: 431-432); Woleaian and Chuukese made them separate phonemes, Kiribati merged [ɨ] with i (p. 94). Chuukese changes in §§2.3.1-2.3.9 with 126 numbered cognate sets in the Appendix (pp. 104-113). Chuukese vowels written i ú u e é o á a ó (IPA i ɨ u e ə o æ a ɔ).
